results.title: Passages of a non-review source still name the brand

steps.title: Given the user is on Actions Center > Target Sources of analysis A
When the user opens the panel of the non-review source and selects the tab "Negative perception"
And the user reads the passage of each article
Then every passage contains the brand or one of its product names

results.notes: Toyota 439acd96, Last 7 days, AI Engines (4: gemini, grok, openai, perplexity), All Countries. Cards shown with tabs ALL / IMPROVE VISIBILITY / IMPROVE PERCEPTION. guideautoweb.com (#1, badge Journalism): Negative perception (7) = 7 article rows, no page block, 1 passage each; every passage names Toyota or a model (Toyota, Toyota Venza, Toyota RAV4, Toyota C-HR), brand highlighted. Extra API check (read-only GET of the panel endpoint): 102/102 NAMED_NEGATIVELY passages on the 38 non-Review-Sites sources of the analysis contain their matchedEntity; none grouped, none without passage.

results.title: Comparison page on a Review Sites domain keeps one passage naming the brand

steps.title: Given the user is on Actions Center > Target Sources of analysis A
When the user opens the panel of the source and selects the tab "Negative perception"
Then the comparison page shows one passage
And the passage names the brand

results.notes: Orange 16cdf040 (default filters Last 7 days, AI Engines gemini + openai, All Countries). choisir.com (#16, badge Review Sites): Negative perception (1) lists the comparison page "Liste des opérateurs mobiles en France | Choisir.com" (/forfait-mobile/operateurs) with ONE classic passage naming Orange ("…plusieurs scandales… sur des parts de marché conclu entre Orange"); no review entries, no chip (API grouped=false, reviewCount=0, pages=[]). degrouptest.com (Review Sites) comparison / news articles are also classic (4 negative, 1 passage each, all name Orange). results.title: GEO-1224 no title, menu, cookie banner or favourable sentence on non-review sources

steps.title: Given the user is on Actions Center > Target Sources of analysis A
When the user opens the panels of edmunds, alvolante, frandroid and caradisiac and selects "Negative perception"
Then no passage is a page title, a cookie banner, a menu or a favourable sentence
And a criticism far from the brand name is joined to the nearest brand name with "…"

results.notes: The step wording names edmunds / alvolante / frandroid / caradisiac, but on staging 2026-11-03 edmunds.com is Review Sites and alvolante.it / frandroid.com are not in the Last 7 days list: only caradisiac.com (Journalism, #33) could be used (test data cell). caradisiac: Negative perception (1) = /avis/ with the quote "Un SUV en occasion : le Toyota Rav-4 de 3e génération aurait-il été le pire des Rav-4 en matière de fiabilité ?" = a criticism of the RAV4, not the page title ("Retrouvez tous les avis..."), not a banner or menu; it is the teaser headline of a linked article on the listing page (checked in the page HTML). Step 4: no far-away criticism on caradisiac (the join does not apply there); the "{brand} … {criticism}" join is visible on other Journalism sources of the same analysis (autoplus.fr "… Toyota applique en revanche des tarifs élevés", automobile-magazine.fr "Toyota Yaris Cross… 116h : Un rappel…", caranddriver.com "Toyota… LOWS: …"), see step4_join. PARTIAL because 3 of the 4 named sources are not usable. Cross-reference: the GEO-1224 header defect found on automobile-magazine.fr is reported in TC-GEO-1547-025.

results.title: GEO-1201 passage cut at 140 characters on a whole word on non-review sources

steps.title: Given the user is on Actions Center > Target Sources of analysis A
When the user opens a Journalism source panel with a passage ending with "…"
Then the passage is at most 140 characters including "…"
And it ends on a whole word with one single "…" character

results.notes: guideautoweb.com: passages ending with "…" are 139, 139, 137, 139 and 132 characters ("…" included, quotes excluded), ending on whole words ("a…", "aux…", "dont…", "les…", "doute…") with one single "…". automobile-magazine.fr: the 3 "…" passages (136, 139, 137 chars) were checked against the live page HTML - the cut is always followed by a space in the source ("conduite| bien utile", "se| couper", "peut| être"), so no cut word. API sweep of the 102 non-review passages: max length 140, no "……". Observations outside the TC data: caranddriver.com "...real-world testing.…" and motorbiscuit.com "...happy drivers.…" end with a full stop followed by "…"; autoblog.com ends with ASCII "..." at 130 chars (likely the source text, not a cut).
